page: The Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. It incorporates 16.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio typical of general-purpose sizing, and includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for scratch files and ephemeral data. Hardware vectorization support includes AVX-512 foundation, VNNI, and BF16 instructions, running atop Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal pronounced single-threaded processing capabilities alongside modest parallel throughput. The instance achieves strong scores in single-core metrics, registering 3079.47 on stress-ng and 1987.0 in Geekbench, placing it in the upper quartile for single-thread responsiveness. Conversely, multi-core metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 4447.0 and PassMark extended instruction score of 5349.07, reflect the physical two-core constraint. Memory bandwidth registers at 37.93 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 28.17 GB/sec for writes. Application-specific benchmarks show static web serving throughput of 6.43 GB/sec and Redis SET throughput of 5.92 million operations per second, with smaller language model processing executing at 472.27 prompt tokens per second.

Given its hardware profile and test results, the D4ads_v6 provides balanced cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing per-thread CPU performance over deep multi-threaded scalability. The presence of integrated local NVMe storage reduces network storage dependency for temporary caching, build artifacts, and intermediate pipelines. Appropriate workloads include static and dynamic web servers, continuous integration agents, text and log processing pipelines, and mid-tier staging or development environments. Applications reliant on massive parallel database scaling or large-model AI inference are limited by the physical core count and lower memory bandwidth.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V and the x86_64 architecture, it features AVX-512 extensions and dedicated CPU allocation. Benchmark performance demonstrates strong single-core execution, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1987.0 and stress-ng score of 3079.47. However, multi-core capacity and uncached memory bandwidth reside in lower tiers due to the two-core hardware ceiling. The server achieves 6.43 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and handles light AI inference effectively. With a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio and bundled high-speed local disk, the D4ads_v6 fits general-purpose cloud duties, web hosting, intermediate text processing, and CI/CD compilation tasks.
